data.name: Asa
data.gender_notes: Asa is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew ‘asah’, meaning ‘to heal’. In the Bible, Asa was a king of Judah who ruled in the late 9th and early 8th centuries BC. He is remembered for his faith and religious reforms. The name ‘Asa’ is also associated with the healing power of God. The name Asa carries the meaning “God's healer” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Asa usually hope their child will grow to embody god's healer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Asa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's healer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asa total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Asa was a king of Judah, reigning from approximately 911 to 870 BCE. He is considered one of the early good kings of Judah, bringing about religious reforms and military successes.
Asa also appears in the New Testament, specifically in the book of Acts, as one of the early converts to Christianity. He was a proconsul of Achaia, living in Corinth around 49 CE.

modern_usage.modern_context:

In the Bible, Asa is the name of a king of Judah who ruled from 911 to 870 BC. He is known for his faith in God, his military victories, and his religious reforms. Asa's story is a popular one in religious communities and has led to the name being used in various religious contexts.

Additionally, the name Asa has become popular in the context of minimalist names or names with simple meanings. Social media platforms have seen an increase in the use of the name Asa as users look for unique and meaningful names for their profiles.

Babynames.com, a popular website for expecting parents, has reported an uptick in searches for the name Asa in recent years. Overall, the name Asa is a timeless and meaningful choice that appeals to those seeking names with historical or biblical significance.
